images.filename: Adam and Eve on Tryfan - geograph.org.uk - 57522.jpg
images.caption: Adam and Eve on Tryfan. These 2 standing stones are the very highest point on the top centre of Tryfan. On a still day, the brave will climb them and jump the gap, which is wider than it looks at this angle. Fortunately it was horrendously windy, so I didn't have the option.

images.filename: A5 and Llyn Ogwen from Tryfan's North Ridge - geograph.org.uk - 71613.jpg
images.caption: A5 and Llyn Ogwen from Tryfan's North Ridge. The best way up Tryfan is of course by the direct route up the north ridge which has some difficult scrambling in places. This shot was taken from a third of the way up looking down on Llyn Ogwen and the A5. Being early morning at 07:21, the normal throng of cars and people had not yet materialised.

images.filename: Awyrlun o Gastell y Bere yn Hydref 2024 - Aerial image of Welsh castle Castell y Bere near Tywyn, Gwynedd, Wales 50.png
images.caption:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
Castell y Bere is a Welsh castle in south Gwynedd, Wales. It was one of the most important castles of the princes of Gwynedd in the 13th century. It was built by Llywelyn the Great to keep out the invading English. It is believed that the poet Gruffudd ab yr Ynad Goch composed his famous elegy for Prince Llywelyn ap Gruffudd (Llywelyn II) in Castell y Bere in December 1282 or early 1283.
images.alt:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
